task\\u0027s pull request was carried by 2 runs. Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 2 \\u00B7 6ec9001c]\\n\\n- **What exists now:** \\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Transport/\\u0060 has the export (\\u0060LedgerExport\\u0060, \\u0060LedgerRefs\\u0060, \\u0060LedgerSegments\\u0060, \\u0060LedgerLine\\u0060, \\u0060LedgerOrigin\\u0060). \\u0060FieldDeclaration.Tag\\u0060 and \\u0060ParcelType.TagField\\u0060 mark the tag field. Signed lines now carry \\u0060event\\u0060 and \\u0060recorded\\u0060. The daemon registers \\u0060LedgerExport\\u0060, and the loop runs only when \\u0060DaemonOptions.ExportInterval\\u0060 is set (the CLI uses 15 seconds). \\u0060PublishAsync(project)\\u0060 exports and pushes one project at once and returns a \\u0060LedgerPublication\\u0060 listing any failures.\\n- **For the importer:** write a \\u0060LedgerLine\\u0060 per received line, with \\u0060Id\\u0060 set to the event id, the line as received, its own segment, and \\u0060StoreSequence\\u0060 set to the local sequence after appending. The export then skips that event. Append the event with the line\\u0027s stream, event id, and recorded time. Lines are verified one by one, not by commit history, and a rebuilt local ref doesn\\u0027t share commits with the remote.\\n- **Gotchas:** the scanned-past position is in memory only, so each start re-reads from each project\\u0027s last line once. Fisher\\u0027s typed read silently skips event types this build doesn\\u0027t know.\\n- **Left undone on purpose:** filtering pushes by tag (every repo carries the whole chain in phase 3), forwarding, any \\u0060coa\\u0060 command for export, and carrying an old node identity forward, which belongs to the rebuild task. Decision \\u0060f11d3247\\u0060 needs a human to supersede it.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 2 \\u00B7 fe8f1375]\\n\\n- I added commit \\u00600ed0b26\\u0060 on the PR branch. \\u0060DaemonInfo.Load\\u0060 now opens \\u0060daemon.json\\u0060 so it tolerates the daemon writing or deleting the file at the same time, and a missing or half-written file reads as null (no daemon yet). The new \\u0060tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/DaemonInfoTests.cs\\u0060 covers this.\\n- macOS ignores file sharing rules, so the half-written-file test only proves anything on Windows CI. Treat the Windows run of PR 73 as the real check.\\n- I left one possible flaky test alone: a single failure in \\u0060WorktreeStepTests.InitializeAsync\\u0060 that didn\\u0027t come back. Its error message wasn\\u0027t captured, so I had nothing to act
